VERDICT: CLEAN

BOUNDARY: Checked the support endpoints \(x=\pm1\). The function is zero outside \([-1,1]\) and positive inside. At \(\pm1\) the one‑sided derivatives from the interior are finite sums of derivatives of \(\phi\) at \(0\); all those derivatives vanish, so they match the identically zero exterior. Hence \(b\) is \(C^\infty\) everywhere. The set where \(b\neq0\) is exactly \((-1,1)\); its closure in \(\mathbb{R}\) is \([-1,1]\), which is the support. No degenerate or counterexample cases were found; the zero, one, and endpoint checks all pass.

- `ex-flat-exponential-function` (defines the flat \(\phi\) and its derivatives at \(0\)),

- `def-metric-interior-closure-boundary` (definition of closure used for support).
Each supplies exactly the facts needed; no mismatches or missing hypotheses.

CHECKED: Title, public claim (“smooth, positive on \((-1,1)\), zero outside \([-1,1]\); support \([-1,1]\)”), every numbered step (1.1, 1.2, 2.1), and Remarks (none present). The reasoning is valid and the conclusion holds.
